content_sections.title: Read four bounded events
content_sections.body_text: Background: ‘I was walking to class.’ Four events follow: (1) ‘First, it began to rain.’ (2) ‘Next, a strong gust turned my umbrella inside out.’ (3) ‘Then, I made a decision to wait in the library.’ (4) ‘Finally, when the rain eased, I continued to class.’

content_sections.title: Notice order and combination
content_sections.body_text: Draw a long line for was walking. Then number only the four marked events 1–4 and underline first, next, then, and finally. Circle made a decision: English conventionally combines make with decision. The background sets the scene; the four markers bound the sequence.

content_sections.title: Signal information focus
content_sections.body_text: Relative prominence marks the new or contrasting information: ‘I waited in the LIBRARY, not the café.’ Make LIBRARY clearer and stronger than nearby words. Change the place to HOME; the strongest word changes because the intended contrast changes.

content_sections.title: Transform, retell, verify
content_sections.body_text: Change the place and weather problem, but keep one background plus exactly four numbered events. Include all four order markers and make a decision, then retell without reading. Check: there are four—not three or five—events, the weather wording is natural, the lexical combination is intact, and one contrast word is prominent.
